questions.question: How do grid tracks, lines, and cells define a CSS Grid layout?
questions.title: CSS Grid tracks, lines, and cells
questions.direct_answer: A Grid container is divided by numbered or named grid lines. The space between two neighbouring lines is a track—a row or column—and the intersection of one row track with one column track is a cell. Grid items are placed by line positions and may span several cells, while gutters created by gap are separate from the tracks.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether the learner understands Grid vocabulary well enough to reason about placement.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Calling grid items or gaps tracks, or forgetting that N tracks create N plus one lines.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Connect line placement to source-order accessibility and implicit track creation.

sections.title: Quick revision
items: Grid lines form the boundaries used for placement.
A track is one row or one column between adjacent lines.
A cell is one row-track and column-track intersection.
An item can span multiple tracks by naming its start and end lines.

sections.title: Interview answer
sections.content:
CSS Grid creates a two-dimensional coordinate system inside a grid container. grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows define tracks, and grid lines form the boundaries before, between, and after those tracks.

If a grid has three columns, it has four column lines. An item can be placed from column line 1 to line 3, so it spans the first two column tracks. The same rule applies to rows, and negative line numbers can count backward from the end of the explicit grid.

A grid cell is the smallest area formed by one row track and one column track. A grid area is any rectangle covering one or more cells. gap adds gutters between tracks; it does not create an extra track that items can occupy.

For example, a page shell can define two columns named sidebar and content, then make its header span from the first to the last column line. Named areas can make the same placement easier to read when the layout represents recognisable regions.

One boundary is source order. Visual grid placement does not change the document order used by keyboard navigation and many assistive technologies, so the HTML should remain logical before CSS rearranges it. Named lines and named areas improve maintainability when numbers stop communicating intent. The underlying model remains the same: every named boundary still resolves to a grid line, and every area remains a rectangle bounded by lines.

sections.title: A coordinate system made from boundaries
sections.content: Lines are addresses, tracks are the sized strips between addresses, cells are their smallest intersections, and areas are rectangles made from cells. Once these terms are separate, placement declarations such as grid-column: 1 / 3 become simple boundary instructions.

sections.title: Explicit placement and automatic placement share the same grid
sections.content: Items with line or area placement occupy their requested cells first. Remaining items enter the auto-placement algorithm and fill available positions according to grid-auto-flow. If placement requests a line beyond the explicit template, the browser creates implicit tracks, so an apparently simple line number can also change the layout's size.

sections.title: Three columns create four column lines
sections.content:
line 1      line 2      line 3      line 4
  | track 1   | track 2   | track 3   |
  |   cell    |   cell    |   cell    |  row track
  |----------- gap is between tracks -----------|

sections.title: Place regions by grid line
sections.content:
```html
Site header spans both tracks
Topics
Lesson
``` The two column tracks have three lines. The header starts at line 1 and ends at -1, the final explicit line.

questions.question: What is the difference between an explicit grid and an implicit grid?
questions.title: Explicit and implicit CSS Grid
questions.direct_answer: The explicit grid contains rows and columns declared with grid-template-rows, grid-template-columns, or grid-template-areas. The implicit grid contains extra tracks the browser creates when auto-placed content needs more room or an item is placed beyond the explicit lines. grid-auto-rows and grid-auto-columns size those generated tracks.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether the learner can explain where undeclared grid tracks come from.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Assuming every visible row is explicit or overlooking an accidental implicit column.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Mention negative lines and use a Grid overlay to verify the actual track structure.

sections.title: Quick revision
items: Template properties create the explicit grid.
Overflowing placement or additional content creates implicit tracks.
Implicit tracks are auto-sized unless grid-auto-* changes them.
Unexpected implicit columns often reveal an incorrect line placement.

sections.title: Interview answer
sections.content:
The explicit grid is the track structure written in the stylesheet. If grid-template-columns declares three columns and grid-template-rows declares two rows, those six cells belong to the explicit grid.

The implicit grid extends that structure when the content cannot fit or placement asks for a location outside it. For example, a seventh auto-placed card creates another row, and an item placed at grid-column: 5 creates columns beyond a three-column template.

Generated tracks use automatic sizing by default. grid-auto-rows and grid-auto-columns let the design control them, such as giving every automatically created row a minimum height.

This behaviour is useful because a list can grow without declaring the exact number of rows. It is also a debugging clue: a mysterious narrow column at the edge often means an item referenced the wrong line and caused an implicit column.

The boundary is that negative line numbers refer to the end of the explicit grid, not the ever-growing implicit grid. When exact placement matters, I inspect the Grid overlay and verify both the requested lines and the auto-flow direction.

sections.title: Declared tracks and generated tracks
sections.content: An explicit template states the intended skeleton. The implicit grid is the browser's extension mechanism for content or placement beyond that skeleton. Both sets of tracks participate in layout, but different properties size them.

sections.title: Automatic rows are common; accidental columns are suspicious
sections.content: A card gallery normally declares columns and lets rows appear as content grows, so implicit rows are expected. An implicit column is more likely to come from grid-auto-flow: column or an out-of-range grid-column value. Developer Tools can label explicit and implicit lines, making the source of the extra track visible.

sections.title: Who creates and sizes each grid
sections.content:
| Grid part | Created by | Sized by |
|---|---|---|
| Explicit tracks | Template declarations | grid-template-columns / rows |
| Implicit tracks | Extra content or out-of-range placement | grid-auto-columns / rows |

sections.title: Control automatically created rows

questions.question: How do minmax(), auto-fit, and auto-fill create responsive CSS grids?
questions.title: Responsive Grid with minmax, auto-fit, and auto-fill
questions.direct_answer: repeat() can create as many tracks as fit, while minmax() gives each track a lower and upper size. auto-fit collapses unused repeated tracks so existing items stretch into the space; auto-fill keeps empty tracks reserved. A common fluid pattern is repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 14rem), 1fr)).

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether the learner can explain responsive track repetition instead of copying a one-line recipe.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using a fixed minmax minimum that is wider than the container or confusing auto-fit with auto-fill.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Explain the empty-track difference and the cases that still deserve a media query.

sections.title: Quick revision
items: minmax sets a permitted minimum and maximum track size.
auto-fit collapses empty repeated tracks.
auto-fill keeps empty repeated tracks in the grid.
The minimum must not be wider than a very narrow container.

sections.title: Interview answer
sections.content:
A responsive Grid can let the available container width decide the column count instead of switching at named device widths. repeat with auto-fit or auto-fill asks the browser to create as many repeated tracks as can fit.

minmax supplies a range for each track. In minmax(14rem, 1fr), a card should not become narrower than 14rem while spare space is shared through 1fr. Wrapping occurs when another minimum-width track no longer fits.

auto-fit and auto-fill behave similarly while enough items fill every track. When the row has fewer items, auto-fit collapses empty tracks and lets occupied tracks expand. auto-fill preserves empty tracks, so the available positions remain even when no item occupies them.

For example, repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 14rem), 1fr)) creates a gallery that becomes one column when its container is narrower than 14rem. The inner min prevents the minimum track from overflowing that narrow container.

The boundary is design intent. A media query is still appropriate when the component needs a qualitative change, such as moving controls or changing navigation behaviour. Auto-fit solves fluid track count; it does not decide every responsive interaction. I verify the pattern with unusually long titles and with browser zoom, not only evenly sized placeholder cards. Intrinsic content can raise a track's practical minimum and expose assumptions that a clean demo does not show.

sections.title: Let track constraints create the breakpoint
sections.content: The grid wraps at the width where another track's minimum plus its gap no longer fits. That breakpoint comes from the content's usable minimum rather than a device label. The maximum 1fr value then stretches the tracks to consume each row.

sections.title: Empty-track behaviour separates fit from fill
sections.content: auto-fill fills the available row with track slots even when some slots are empty. auto-fit first creates the possible slots, then collapses empty ones. With enough cards there is no visible difference. Test with one or two cards in a wide container to see which behaviour matches the design.

sections.title: Wide container with two cards
sections.content:
auto-fill: [card][card][empty][empty]
auto-fit:  [   card   ][   card   ]
Both wrap when another minimum-size track cannot fit.

sections.title: A fluid card gallery without device breakpoints

questions.question: When should you use CSS Grid instead of Flexbox?
questions.title: Choosing CSS Grid or Flexbox
questions.direct_answer: Use CSS Grid when items need to share both row and column tracks, when regions have named two-dimensional positions, or when alignment must continue across rows. Use Flexbox when one row or column should flow mainly from its content. Grid and Flexbox are complementary and can be nested inside the same component.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether the learner chooses Grid for actual two-dimensional constraints.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using wrapped Flexbox and expecting columns on separate lines to align.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Identify shared tracks as the signal and acknowledge normal flow as another valid option.

sections.title: Quick revision
items: Grid coordinates two dimensions and shared tracks.
Flexbox distributes items along one main axis.
Wrapped flex lines do not share column widths.
Use normal flow when no special axis relationship is needed.

sections.title: Interview answer
sections.content:
I choose CSS Grid when the design has a two-dimensional relationship. If cards must line up on common columns across several rows, or page regions belong in named row-and-column positions, shared grid tracks express that structure directly.

I choose Flexbox when the relationship is mainly one-dimensional and content should drive the sizes. A toolbar, group of actions, or media object usually needs distribution along one row or one column rather than a full coordinate system.

For example, a pricing table whose feature names and plan values must align across rows belongs in Grid. A row of buttons inside each plan can still use Flexbox for spacing and alignment.

Wrapped Flexbox is not equivalent to Grid: every flex line distributes its own space independently, so columns on different lines may not align. Grid keeps items attached to shared tracks.

The boundary is simplicity. A normal block flow already handles headings and paragraphs well, and a one-column page does not need Grid merely because Grid is available. I use the layout mode that makes the important relationship obvious in the stylesheet.

sections.title: Shared tracks are the deciding signal
sections.content: If a line drawn through one row or column should also align items in other rows or columns, Grid provides that shared track. If each line can size itself independently, Flexbox is usually enough.

sections.title: Grid and Flexbox constraint models
sections.content: Grid is layout-led: tracks and areas often express the desired structure before content is placed. Flexbox is content-led: item bases and free space often determine the final line. Real components combine them freely, such as a Grid page shell containing Flexbox navigation and form-action rows.

sections.title: Layout relationship comparison
sections.content:
| Question | Grid | Flexbox |
|---|---|---|
| Shared columns across rows? | Yes | No, lines are independent |
| One content-led toolbar? | Possible, often more than needed | Ideal |
| Named page regions? | Ideal | Awkward |
| Align controls inside one card? | Possible | Usually ideal |

sections.title: Keep shared feature columns aligned
sections.content:
```html
Feature
Basic
Pro
Storage
5 GB
50 GB
``` Every row uses the same three tracks, so feature values remain aligned vertically.

questions.question: Why can Grid items overflow or create unexpected columns?
questions.title: Debugging CSS Grid overflow and implicit columns
questions.direct_answer: Grid overflow usually comes from track minimums or item placement. A 1fr track still has an automatic minimum that can preserve wide content, fixed minimum tracks may exceed the container, and placement beyond the explicit grid creates implicit columns. Use minmax(0, 1fr), min-width: 0, responsive minimums, and corrected line placement according to the actual cause.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether the learner can separate intrinsic track sizing from implicit-track placement bugs.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Assuming 1fr can never overflow or clipping the entire page without finding the offending track.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Use a Grid overlay and pair minmax(0, 1fr) with a content-specific response.

sections.title: Quick revision
items: 1fr shares free space but does not automatically erase min-content minimums.
Out-of-range grid placement creates implicit tracks.
Fixed track minimums can exceed a narrow container.
Inspect the Grid overlay before hiding overflow.

sections.title: Interview answer
sections.content:
When a Grid overflows, I inspect both the track definitions and the items placed into them. A fractional track shares available free space, but its automatic minimum can still be based on min-content. A long unbroken string, table, or wide child may therefore hold the track open.

minmax(0, 1fr) explicitly allows a fractional track to shrink below that content-based minimum. min-width: 0 on the grid item can release a similar item-level constraint, followed by a deliberate wrapping or scrolling rule for its content.

Fixed minimums can cause another problem. repeat(auto-fit, minmax(18rem, 1fr)) cannot fit inside a container narrower than 18rem, so min(100%, 18rem) is safer when the component may be embedded in a narrow region.

Unexpected columns usually come from placement. For example, grid-column: 4 on a two-column explicit grid asks the browser to create implicit tracks up to that line. A Grid overlay exposes those generated lines immediately.

I avoid overflow: hidden as the first fix because it can clip content and focus indicators. The boundary is intentionally wide content such as a data table; that content may need its own labelled horizontal scroller instead of forcing the whole page wider. Direction-aware inspection also matters: logical inline overflow may appear on either physical side in different writing modes. Fixing the sizing constraint instead of a left-or-right symptom keeps the component portable.

sections.title: Track constraints and placement are separate causes
sections.content: A grid can grow because a track refuses to become smaller or because an item asks for a track that did not exist. First inspect computed track sizes, then inspect each item's line placement. That keeps a content-size fix from masking a placement error.

sections.title: Fractional does not mean unconstrained
sections.content: The minimum of a plain 1fr track is effectively auto, so intrinsic content still participates. minmax(0, 1fr) changes that minimum, but the content then needs a readable response. For unexpected tracks, compare the explicit line count with each grid-row and grid-column declaration, including negative and named lines.

sections.title: Grid overflow diagnosis
sections.content:
Grid is too wide
  -> Track computed wider than container?
       -> intrinsic minimum -> minmax(0, 1fr) plus content handling
       -> fixed minimum -> make minimum container-safe
  -> Extra track visible?
       -> inspect grid-column and grid-auto-flow

sections.title: Let the content track become genuinely flexible
sections.content:
```html
Menu
one-very-long-unbroken-resource-name
``` The second track may shrink below the link's min-content width, while the link has an explicit wrapping rule.
